title: Zellweger syndrome: peroxisome biogenesis defect (VLCFA + phytanic acid up)
vignette: A 4-month-old infant is evaluated for hypotonia, poor feeding, and seizures. The infant has dysmorphic craniofacial features, including a high forehead and a broad nasal bridge, and hepatomegaly is present. There is profound developmental delay. Laboratory studies show markedly elevated very-long-chain fatty acids and elevated phytanic acid in the blood. A defect in which of the following organelles is most likely responsible for this patient's condition?

clues.note: Severe hypotonia, feeding difficulty, and seizures in early infancy with dysmorphism suggest a metabolic/genetic disorder affecting the brain.
Elevated VLCFAs indicate failed peroxisomal beta-oxidation - the peroxisome is where VLCFAs are normally shortened.
Elevated phytanic acid reflects impaired peroxisomal ALPHA-oxidation; together with high VLCFAs it points to a global peroxisomal defect (Zellweger).

whatMatters: An infant with hypotonia, seizures, craniofacial dysmorphism, hepatomegaly, and BOTH elevated very-long-chain fatty acids AND phytanic acid = Zellweger syndrome, a peroxisome biogenesis disorder (PEX gene mutations). The defective organelle is the PEROXISOME, which normally performs VLCFA beta-oxidation and phytanic acid alpha-oxidation. Answer D.
strategy: Let the two lab abnormalities localize the organelle: VLCFA beta-oxidation and phytanic acid alpha-oxidation both occur in peroxisomes, so elevations of both = peroxisomal failure (Zellweger). Reject lysosomes (accumulate substrates like sphingolipids/mucopolysaccharides, normal VLCFA), mitochondria (medium/long-chain FA oxidation), and other organelles.

eliminations.label: Golgi apparatus - trafficking, not fatty-acid oxidation
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the Golgi modifies and sorts proteins/lipids (e.g., glycosylation). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it does not oxidize VLCFAs or phytanic acid; a Golgi defect would not raise these. ✅ Correct if: protein glycosylation/trafficking disorders (e.g., I-cell disease affects mannose-6-phosphate tagging).

eliminations.label: Lysosomes - storage disorders, normal VLCFA (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: lysosomes degrade macromolecules; defects cause storage diseases (sphingolipidoses, mucopolysaccharidoses). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: lysosomal disorders accumulate their specific substrates, not VLCFAs/phytanic acid, which are peroxisomal. ✅ Correct if: e.g., Tay-Sachs, Gaucher, Hurler with accumulated lysosomal substrate.

eliminations.label: Mitochondria - short/medium/long-chain FA oxidation
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: mitochondria beta-oxidize short-, medium-, and long-chain fatty acids. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: VERY-long-chain fatty acids require peroxisomal beta-oxidation first; a mitochondrial defect (e.g., MCAD) elevates medium-chain acyl products, not VLCFA/phytanic acid. ✅ Correct if: MCAD deficiency (hypoketotic hypoglycemia).

eliminations.label: Proteasomes - protein degradation
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: proteasomes degrade ubiquitin-tagged proteins. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: unrelated to fatty-acid metabolism; would not raise VLCFA/phytanic acid. ✅ Correct if: ubiquitin-proteasome degradation questions.

eliminations.label: Smooth ER - lipid/steroid synthesis and detox
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the smooth ER synthesizes lipids/steroids and detoxifies drugs. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it does not perform VLCFA beta-oxidation or phytanic acid alpha-oxidation. ✅ Correct if: steroid synthesis or cytochrome P450 detox questions.

reasoning: Infant with hypotonia, seizures, dysmorphism, hepatomegaly + elevated VLCFA AND phytanic acid
Peroxisomes perform VLCFA beta-oxidation and phytanic acid alpha-oxidation
Both elevated = global peroxisomal failure = Zellweger syndrome (peroxisome biogenesis disorder)
mechanism: Peroxisomes are membrane-bound organelles that carry out the beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids (shortening them for further mitochondrial oxidation), the alpha-oxidation of branched-chain phytanic acid, and the synthesis of plasmalogens (important myelin lipids). Zellweger syndrome (cerebrohepatorenal syndrome) is a peroxisome BIOGENESIS disorder caused by mutations in PEX genes, which encode peroxins needed to assemble functional peroxisomes; without them, peroxisomal enzymes are not properly imported and multiple peroxisomal functions fail simultaneously. The result is accumulation of very-long-chain fatty acids and phytanic acid, deficient plasmalogens, and severe early disease: profound hypotonia, seizures, craniofacial dysmorphism, hepatomegaly, and developmental delay, usually fatal in infancy. Because BOTH VLCFA and phytanic acid are elevated (pointing to a global peroxisomal defect rather than a single-enzyme deficiency like X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy, which raises VLCFA alone), the culprit organelle is the peroxisome.

difficulty.label: 📚 Pure knowledge gap
difficulty.message: First Aid Biochem (cell) > peroxisome: beta-oxidation of VLCFA, alpha-oxidation of phytanic acid, plasmalogen synthesis; Zellweger (PEX genes) = biogenesis defect; contrast Refsum (phytanic acid) and X-ALD (VLCFA).

difficulty.label: 🧭 Understanding the question
difficulty.message: Two elevated peroxisomal substrates (VLCFA + phytanic acid) localize the defect to the peroxisome (Zellweger).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocabulary
difficulty.message: Unsure on VLCFA, phytanic acid, alpha- vs beta-oxidation, peroxisome, PEX genes, or plasmalogen? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🧲 Pulled by a distractor
difficulty.message: Lysosomes (storage disorders), mitochondria (medium/long-chain FA), Golgi/proteasome/smooth ER don't handle VLCFA + phytanic acid.

difficulty.label: ✍️ Something else
difficulty.message: Bank: Zellweger = peroxisome biogenesis defect (PEX), ↑VLCFA + ↑phytanic acid; Refsum = phytanic acid; X-ALD = VLCFA.
